blocks.text: Alexander Brest Gallery at Jacksonville University presents Hold Me Tight , a solo exhibition by Nashville-based artist Chrissy Lush , on view November 19, 2026 through January 14, 2027. The exhibition marks the first presentation of Hold Me Tight as a solo exhibition. Through a series of constructed self-portraits, Lush explores the tension between memory and identity and the psychological experience of approaching middle age.

Created between 2019 and 2022, Hold Me Tight grew out of Lush’s changing perception of herself as she approached forty: an internal sense of herself as a young woman increasingly at odds with the person she saw in the mirror. Against the broader cultural glorification of youth, the work considers the unease of aging alongside the persistent attachment to earlier versions of ourselves.

Through digital compositing, Lush brings younger and present selves together in imagined encounters. The photographs return to activities and experiences associated with youth—childhood games, sunbathing, climbing trees—not as literal reconstructions of particular memories, but as evocations of the freedom and vitality with which the past can become invested. Moving between scenes of connection and solitude, Hold Me Tight occupies the space between nostalgia and reality, examining how memory shapes our understanding of who we were and who we have become.

Lush’s work has recently received growing national and international recognition. In 2026, her work was presented in a solo booth at The Photography Show presented by AIPAD at the Park Avenue Armory in New York. Three of her photographs were shortlisted for the 2026 Aesthetica Art Prize and are currently included in States of Becoming at York Art Gallery in the United Kingdom. Her work has appeared in Aesthetica Magazine , Border Crossings and Observer and is held in public and private collections, including the Møller Collection in Oslo.

Chrissy Lush is a Nashville-based artist working primarily in photography. She received her MFA in Photography from Parsons School of Design and her BFA in Photography from SUNY Purchase. Her practice explores the ways we construct our realities and how we function within those constructs.
